rationale: C13 plausibly supplied the concrete drafting template for the child's second operative paragraph. It contains the same detailed employee-excusal machinery, including the two exceptions, the declaration that the excused period is a holiday, the same masked June 9, 1952 directive reference, and the same compensation-and-leave clause. The child adapts that language from metropolitan and field employees on two half-days to federal employees on the Isthmus of Panama on the memorial-dedication day. C20 and C23 contain earlier versions of the employee-excusal formula but lack C13's especially probative holiday-reference language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: except those who may for special public reasons be excluded from the provisions of this order by the heads of their respective departments, establishments, or agencies, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent with the provisions of existing law, shall be excused from duty on March 31, 1954
shared_material.parent_excerpt: except those who may for special public reasons be excluded from the provisions of this order by the heads of their respective departments, establishments, or agencies, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent with the provisions of existing law, shall be excused from duty on such one-half days
shared_material.explanation: This is a lengthy, nearly verbatim replication of the operative excusal rule and its two exceptions, with only the affected date and employee group adapted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: such day shall be considered a holiday on the Isthmus of Panama within the meaning of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 9, 1952, and of all statutes so far as they relate to the compensation and leave of employees of the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: each such one-half day shall be considered a holiday within the meaning of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 9, 1952, and of all statutes so far as they relate to the compensation and leave of employees of the United States
shared_material.explanation: The same specific cross-reference and compensation-and-leave legal consequence strongly indicate direct reuse of C13's language.
